page_title: How to Implement a Search Engine Part 2: Query Index

summary.title: How to Implement a Search Engine Part 2: Query Index
summary.one_liner: You learn how to load an inverted index from disk and answer one-word, free-text, and phrase queries using postings lists and positional intersection.
takeaways: Load the index file line by line, splitting on '|', ';', ':' and ',' to rebuild the in-memory dictionary of postings.
One-word queries return the document IDs from the term's postings list, or an empty list if the term is absent.
Free-text queries take the union of the document lists for each query term.
Phrase queries intersect document lists, then subtract i-1 from the i-th term's positions and intersect the position lists to check word order.
Query terms get the same normalization (lowercasing, stopword removal, punctuation removal, stemming) as the indexed collection; results are unranked.
summary.summary: This is the second part of a project series on building a search engine. It assumes an inverted index was previously created and saved to disk, then explains how a query program reads that file back into memory. The post defines three query types (one-word, free-text, and phrase) and gives the algorithm and Python-style pseudocode for each, using a three-document worked example. The phrase query section walks through the positional check in detail, and source code is provided for download.
